#Prevalence
Prevalence of a species refers to the the proportion of samples in which that species is detected.

First we calculate prevalence for all the genera.
```{r}
rel_abund <- prop.table(tax_profile, 2)

rel_abund <- as.data.frame(rel_abund)
rel_abund['prevalence'] <-   apply(rel_abund, 1, function(i) sum(i > 0) / ncol(rel_abund))

which(rel_abund$prevalence == 1) #1,2,11
rownames(rel_abund[c(1,2,11),])

which(rel_abund$prevalence == 0) #100 194 202 228 229 233 236 240 242 244
rownames(rel_abund[c(100,194, 202, 228, 229, 233, 236, 240, 242, 244),])

length(which(rel_abund$prevalence ==min(rel_abund$prevalence[which(rel_abund$prevalence > 0)])))

#Plotted as histogram
prevalence_df <- as.data.frame(rel_abund$prevalence)
colnames(prevalence_df) <- "Prevalence"
prevalence_df$genus <- rownames(rel_abund)

jpeg("hist_prevalence.jpeg")
ggplot(data = prevalence_df) + geom_histogram(mapping = aes(x = Prevalence), bins = 60)
dev.off()
#Most prevalent
head(prevalence_df[order(prevalence_df$Prevalence,decreasing = T),])
#least prevalent
head(prevalence_df[order(prevalence_df$Prevalence,decreasing = F),])
```

```{r}
rel_abund <- rel_abund %>%
  dplyr::filter(prevalence > 0)
pval <- apply(rel_abund[,1:496], 1, function(x) shapiro.test(x)$p.value)
pval <- as.data.frame(pval)
which(pval > 0.05) # 0 are below zero, none are normality distributed

shapiro.test(as.numeric(rel_abund[1,1:496]))$p.value
```

```{r}
length(which(rel_abund[3,1:496] == 0))

zero_genus <- apply(rel_abund, 1, function(x) sum(x==0))
zero_genus <- as.data.frame(zero_genus)
zero_genus$genus <- rownames(zero_genus)

ggplot(zero_genus, aes(x =reorder(genus, -zero_genus), y = zero_genus)) + geom_bar(stat = "identity")

zero_sample <- apply(rel_abund, 2, function(x) sum(x==0))
zero_sample <- as.data.frame(zero_sample)
zero_sample$sampleID <- rownames(zero_sample)
ggplot(zero_sample, aes(x =reorder(sampleID, -zero_sample), y = zero_sample)) + geom_bar(stat = "identity")

```

```{r}
library(vegan)



dist_eucl <- vegdist(t(rel_abund[,1:496]), method = "euclidean")
dist_eucl <- as.matrix(dist_eucl)

#Visualize either with boxplot or with PCoA


rel_ab = prop.table(tax_profile,2)
log_rel_ab = log10(rel_ab+ 10^-4)

n_samples = ncol(log_rel_ab)

# where to save the result
distance = c()
type = c()

# we go through all the pair of samples and we calculate the distance
for(i in c(1: (n_samples-1) )){
  for(j in c( (i+1) : n_samples)){
    # name of the samples
    s_i = colnames(log_rel_ab)[i]
    s_j = colnames(log_rel_ab)[j]
    # profiles
    profile_i = log_rel_ab[,i]
    profile_j = log_rel_ab[,j]
    # calculate the distance as sum of the absolute distance
    d = sum(abs(profile_i - profile_j))
    # add the values
    distance = c(distance,d)
    # add correct type
    if(metadata[s_i,"Subject"] == metadata[s_j,"Subject"]){
      type = c(type,"Within distance")
    }else{
      type = c(type,"Between distance")
    }
  }
}

df = data.frame(dist = distance,type = type)

ggplot(df,aes(type,dist)) + geom_boxplot()


#PCoA
rel_ab <- prop.table(tax_profile,2)
log_rel_ab = log10(rel_ab+ 10^-4)

log_rel_ab = log_rel_ab[rowSums(rel_ab) > 0,]

#prcomp principal component analyisis
pc <- prcomp(t(log_rel_ab),
             center = TRUE,
             scale. = TRUE)

df = data.frame(
  pc1 = pc$x[,1],
  pc2 = pc$x[,2],
  Subject = as.factor(metadata[rownames(pc$x),"Subject"]),
  Timepoint = metadata[rownames(pc$x),"Timepoint"],
  Sex = metadata[rownames(pc$x),"Sex"]
)


ggplot(df,aes(x = pc1,y = pc2, col = Sex)) + geom_point()

ggplot(df,aes(x = pc1,y = pc2, col = Timepoint)) + geom_point()

ggplot(df,aes(x = pc1,y = pc2, col = Subject)) + geom_point() +
theme(legend.position = "none")
```
